evidence: Cic. Div. 2.84: abruptiō corrigiae, a snapped shoelace as a bad omen

phrases.latin: Corrigia tibi solūta est; cavē nē cadās.
phrases.english: Your shoelace is undone; mind you don’t fall.

phrases.latin: Corrigiās tibi ligābō; pedem hūc porrige.
phrases.english: I’ll tie your shoelaces; put your foot out here.

corrigia.against: Lewis & Short corrī^gia, which marks its length as doubtful
corrigia.html: Traupman 117 and Morgan–Owens s.v. shoelace print it unmarked.

sources: Lewis & Short: corrigia · Lewis & Short: solvo · Lewis & Short: ligo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 117, 377.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. shoelace.
